title: The Original Ending of American History X Is Just Fine

commenti.body:
Not calling you a liar or anything, but where is the proof this was the original ending? I swear I saw it on Wikipedia or something at one point, but now I can't find any actual evidence it was the original ending. Is it just urban legend at this point?

And I agree with you! I always thought it would have been a fascinating ending and a gut punch reminder that hate never lets you tie up everything nicely with a little bow and so easily do a 180°
There's definitely a workprint floating around that has the original edit/ ending.

Lamont doesn’t “magically cure” Derek of his racism. The main catalyst for his transformation is his rape at the hands of the people who are “supposed to” be looking out for him, but are simply immersed in a violent, zero-sum struggle for will to power, and it takes him experiencing that violence he had previously inflicted on others to realize just how misguided he was. And on top of that, the only person who is showing him an ounce of humanity during this period is Sweeney, a black man who had also been immersed in the cycle of violence and self-hatred. Sure, you can call Sweeney trope-y, but magnanimous people exist. 

Derek’s transformation has nothing to do with not believing “black people could not be violent criminals”. He’s not naive, he knows that very well, but he recognizes the deep roots of that violence, the fear and the self-preservation and the anger at the injustice of the world, and he chooses not to perpetuate it. And on some level, he knows that Danny’s death is his responsibility, and falling back into the cycle would be the last way to honor him. The “original ending” nullifies that transformation. I’m not saying that anybody is perfect and isn’t subject to the vicissitudes of life, but it’s a completely different story than the director and Norton wanted to tell.

Derek was already disillusioned and disgusted with the gang and that is why they assaulted him. The problem of expecting Derek to be able to own responsibility for his brother death is that when we truly take the concept of cycle of violence serious, responsibility cannot be that clear cut. It's like staying the black criminals like the one who killed Derek's dad needs to realize his part in radicalizing white supremacists.

>The original script, scooped up by my then-partner John Morrissey, ended with the reformed neo-Nazi seeking to avenge his brother’s death. I steadfastly lobbied for moral uplift and redemption, and was able to ensure our film ended with Norton accepting responsibility by uttering, “What have I done?” as he cradles his murdered brother in his arms. It’s a small change, but major to me and, I submit, to the raison d’être of American History X.

So you want to be a producer: Turman, Lawrence

I’m not saying that Derek is explicitly morally responsible for Danny’s death. As you say, it is not that clear cut, but the hatred he’d stoked within Danny led to the friction between him and the shooter and Derek knows he had set him on that path. And as for your last statement, I don’t think it’s as outlandish as you’re making it out to be. Yes, I would say that somebody shooting a firemen would need to realize the amount of ill-will their action is generating if they’re ever going to break out of that cycle. 

There’s no clean “blame” here. It’s an awful cycle of violence that has been perpetuated for millions of years and it takes quite a lot of consciousness to break out of it, which is exactly why they quote Lincoln’s first inaugural at the end of the film.

The original ending doesn't contradict the idea of the Lincoln's quote. It just places a greater divide between our actual belief and the ideals we pay lip service to. The movie isn't saying that being able to realize your own implication is outlandish but it is difficult. And I think that that is a valid idea to entertain. Goodness is not borne out of some uplifting moral lesson. Sometimes you need to live through hell to truly change and another hell may put you back.

I think the ending where the brother is killed by the  African American gang banger he was fueding with is the best 🤷🏼‍♂️ I think it perfectly portrays the cycle of violence - the same story but from the opposite side, both races the same and capable of committing the exact same evil

I don’t really think we’re saying different things to be honest, that’s just not the film that was made. Derek lived through hell and he truly changed. He’s not paying lip service to any ideals. He’s living out an existence in service to the ideals he gathered during his inferno.
